newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sees better ties after Clinton re-election.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sees better ties after Clinton re-election.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam sent a telegram on Wednesday to U.S. President Bill Clinton, welcoming his re-election and expressing hopes for better bilateral ties, Kim's spokeman said.
"I wholeheartedly congratulate your excellency's re-election as the president of the United States," Kim said in the telegram, which was released to reporters.
"I hope our joint efforts to achieve stability and peace on the Korean peninsula will bear fruit in the near future," Kim said.
Clinton and Kim earlier this year jointly proposed four-nation peace talks involving North Korea and China as well as their nations.
The talks are aimed at replacing a truce agreement, that ended the 1950-53 Korean War, with a peace treaty.
Kim said he was satisfied with strong U.S.-South Korean ties and "convinced the alliance of the two countries will strengthen in the future".
The U.S. presidential election was held as the two nations staged a two-week military exercise to improve capabilities to defend against any attack from the communist North.
Hyun Jung-taik, director-general in charge of international economic policy at the Fiance and Economy Ministry, told Reuters that he expected Clinton to take steps to improve trade in Asia.
"With political burden removed by the re-election, I believe President Clinton could allow China to join the World Trade Organisation," he said.
"This coupled with steps to end the yen's weakness will expand trade in Asia. I think Clinton is now free to seek such policies," Hyun added.
Kim's spokesman said the South Korean president is due to telephone Clinton later on Wednesday to personally convey his congratulation.
